facts.text: The clone is a Python driver for a New Focus Picomotor motion controller over USB
The README says the script was tested with a single closed-loop Picomotor controller (model 8745)
The NewFocus command grammar is an optional one-digit driver number, a two-or-more letter mnemonic and an optional numeric parameter
parse_command builds the USB text '1>{driver} {command} {parameter}\r' from a NewFocus command
xPRnn moves motor x by nn steps
The connection check queries motor positions with '1>1 TP?' through '1>4 TP?'
The connect check assumes four motor channels and asks each for its motor type with {m}QM?
The motor-type reply maps 0 to no motor connected, 1 to motor unknown, 2 to 'Tiny' and 3 to 'Standard'
The console reads input with raw_input, which does not exist in Python 3, so start_console is not exposed as a capability
The README directs the reader to section 6.2 of an external 8745 manual for the full command list
The device is found by USB product and vendor ids through usb.core and uses its first IN and OUT endpoints

measures.description: Reported position of motor channels 1 to 4, in controller steps (the TP? query)
measures.name: positions

operator_required.name: move_steps
operator_required.reason: no text file of the clone states how many motor channels the installed controller drives; the upstream connect check polls four channels (newport.py:129-134), which is an assumption of that check, not a bound of the device, so the site sets the channel range

operator_required.name: move_steps
operator_required.reason: no text file of the clone states a travel range or maximum step count; the README names xPRnn without a bound and links the full command list to an external PDF manual (README.md:118), so the site sets the step bound

safe_state.description: all motor movement stopped (the native ST command)
